notes: A 120 V, 1500 W infrared space heater with a fan and a remote control; those figures are for the whole unit, which has one infrared tube and one PTC element. Two versions of the owner's manual differ on the modes (AUTO/HIGH/LOW or ECO/HIGH/LOW) and on low-power wattage, so check the mode button on your unit.

gaps: Manual conflict, modes: the Sylvane copy has AUTO/HIGH/LOW and no per-mode wattage; the Zoro copy has ECO/HIGH/LOW with HIGH 1500 W and LOW 1000 W. Only the Sylvane copy is used for claims.

Manual conflict, other: the Sylvane copy says the standby sensing run is fan only for 30 s every 5 min, under 18 W, and 1.26 kW per hour; the Zoro copy says 40 s of heating and 60 s of fan, no wattage, and 1.35 kW per hour.
Only the Zoro copy shows Thermal Cutoff Protection on the cover and Night mode; only the Sylvane copy has the visual alarm LED.
The 1500 W and 120 V are whole-unit figures; the tube's and the PTC element's own wattage is not given, so v, w and ac are not set on either.
A retailer snippet gave the PTC element 100,000 hours; the manual says 80,000, so the manual figure is used.
Thermal cutoff type, trip temperature, rating and count are not stated (two protection systems are named), so qty and ratings are left out.
The fan motor type (AC or DC) and rating are not stated, so no separate motor part and no ac flag on the fan are claimed.
The 'less than 18 watts' figure is the blower's draw for the standby sensing run; it is kept in the fan spec and not put in w.
The visual alarm's sensor type is not given, so no sensor part is claimed. Cord wire gauge is not given; 12.5 A is the unit's maximum continuous draw.
No OEM part numbers for the tube, PTC element or fan motor were found, and neither manual gives production years.
method: Dr. Infrared Heater owner's manual for the DR-968, 12 pages, PDF on Sylvane's file server (PDF metadata 2015, edited 2018). Its last page gives the maker's name, South San Francisco address, phone and DrHeaterUSA.com, so it is the maker's own manual. Read in full; every claim comes from it.

Dr Heater USA (TLM International) owner's manual for the DR-968 with Advanced Dual Heating System text, 16 pages, PDF on Zoro (PDF metadata April 2021), Burlingame address. Read in full and compared with the Sylvane copy; not used for claims.
The researcher's parts searches found no DR-968 listing for the PTC element, infrared tube or fan motor.

comps.spec: Infrared tube, one per unit, rated for 20,000 hours and up. The manual calls the heating system a far-infrared Quartz-PTC system.
PTC heating element, one per unit, rated for 80,000 hours and up.

Multi-blade turbo blower listed as low noise, with a fan motor factory-lubricated for life. In standby the fan runs alone for 30 seconds every 5 minutes to sense room temperature; the Sylvane copy says that run uses less than 18 watts.
Automatic thermostat, engaged with the AUTO mode. It runs HIGH until the set temperature is reached, then LOW for 10 minutes. Factory default set point 68 F.
Overheat shut-off protection system, plus an inlet-air overheat protection system that shuts the heater off if the air inlet is blocked.
Front panel push buttons (POWER, MODE, Standby ON/OFF, temperature up and down) with an LED display.
Tip-over switch: cuts the heater off when tipped in any direction. The heater works again once returned upright.
Electrostatic air filter at the rear. Clean by vacuuming, monthly or as needed.
Power cord with a grounded three-prong plug.
